question: Why do shop signs in many daguerreotypes read backwards, though negatives made later photographs read true?
options: The lens flipped the picture left to right
The plate was viewed from its lens side
The mercury fumes reversed the silver image
answer: The plate was viewed from its lens side. A lens turns the image upside down, which is only a rotation: turn the plate round and it reads upright. A negative is printed face to face onto paper, which flips it back; a daguerreotype never had that second step.
move: Check whether a fault comes from the tool or from a missing step.
ask: When something looks wrong, is the tool at fault or is a step missing?
trap: Blaming the lens, the part known to invert the picture.
reference: M. Susan Barger & William B. White, The Daguerreotype: Nineteenth-Century Technology and Modern Science, Smithsonian Institution Press, 1991
